notes: The build selection for scripts.game_data.il2cpp.context_audit. These three digests were previously the module-level GA_SHA/MD_SHA/UNITY_SHA constants; they are declarations, not algorithm, so they live here and the module reads them.
GameAssembly.dll and global-metadata.dat gate the audit through scripts.common.check_installed_native_inputs. UnityPlayer.dll is reported and re-hashed by the audit's UnityPlayer consumer checks.
These values match the nativeInputs already recorded by 21 reviewed contracts in this directory for the same installed build.
consumerWindows are the audit's reviewed code windows as [begin RVA, end RVA, SHA256]; they pin the same build as nativeInputs and were moved here from context_audit_common.

pins holds every other build-locked value context_audit checks or reports, grouped by the report key it supports and moved here from context_audit: RVAs, VAs and metadata tokens are 0x-prefixed hex strings, metadata/MethodSpec/generic-instantiation/type indices and counts are integers, and instruction or type-record bytes are bare hex. They pin the same build as nativeInputs; names, IL2CPP structure offsets and element-type tags stay in code because they do not change with a build.

pins.registration.ripReferences rows are [instruction RVA, opcode prefix, target], where the target names codeRegistration (the located CodeRegistration), codeRegistrationGlobal or usageCell. pins.selectedImmediateAdapter.cells rows are [instruction RVA, opcode prefix, usage tag, expected index, role]; the two constructor cells must share one cell.

The context_audit_memorypack, context_audit_skilldata and context_audit_vfs stage modules read pins the same way: sections named selected* are the report key the function's result is published under; SkillData helper sections are named after the helper (skilldataForceSyncReaderEvidence). A value that another section already owns is referenced there rather than repeated. The SkillData reader methods, body windows, observer callsites and source lengths are not repeated here: they are read from skill_cursor_observer_native.json, which must pin the same nativeInputs.
